chapters.summary: After King Ahaziah is injured, he seeks guidance from Baal-zebub instead of the LORD; Elijah prophesies his death, and it comes to pass, showing that the LORD alone is the true God.
keyPoints: Ahaziah falls from the upper chamber of his palace and sends messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub of Ekron.
Elijah delivers the word of the LORD, declaring that Ahaziah will surely die because he has despised God.
Ahaziah twice sends soldiers to seize Elijah, and both companies are consumed by fire from heaven; only the third captain is spared and brought before him.
themes: The true God and false gods
chapters.application: When we face hardship, let us seek God first rather than turning to idols or worldly methods. God is faithful; he will surely guide us and grant us peace.

chapters.summary: Elisha inherits Elijah's prophetic office; he witnesses the Jordan part and Elijah taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, and he performs miracles of healing and judgment.
keyPoints: Before Elijah is taken up to heaven, Elisha follows him closely and asks for a double portion of the spirit that was upon Elijah.
Elisha strikes the water with Elijah's cloak, and the Jordan parts, proving that God is with him.
Elisha heals the bad water at Jericho and curses the youths who mock him, demonstrating the authority of the prophet.
themes: The succession of the prophetic office
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us follow God steadfastly as Elisha did, longing for the power of the Spirit, and bear witness to God's work in our daily lives.

chapters.summary: Moab rebels against Israel, and King Joram joins forces with Judah and Edom to attack Moab; when water runs out on the march, Elisha prays for God to supply water and prophesies victory, and Moab is finally driven back.
keyPoints: Mesha king of Moab rebels against Israel, and King Joram joins with Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom to march against him.
After seven days' march the water runs out, and Joram inquires of Elisha; for Jehoshaphat's sake Elisha asks God to provide water and prophesies victory.
Mistaking the water for blood, the Moabites rush recklessly into battle and are utterly defeated; the king of Moab offers his firstborn son as a sacrifice, and the Israelite army withdraws.
chapters.application: When we face hardship, let us first inquire of God and rely on his promises; he will surely provide living water and victory. Let us act in faith rather than out of rash impulse.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the miracles Elisha performs for the Shunammite woman, the widow of a prophet's disciple, and others, revealing God's great power and care.
keyPoints: Elisha takes pity on a widow deep in debt, causing the last of her oil to keep flowing until there is enough to pay off her debt and save her sons from slavery.
Elisha enables the Shunammite woman to conceive and bear a son, and after the boy dies he raises him back to life.
During a famine Elisha makes a pot of poisonous stew safe to eat, and feeds a hundred men with twenty loaves of bread.
chapters.application: When we are in hardship, let us remember that God cares about every detail of our lives; let us call on him in faith, and he will surely show grace and help.

chapters.summary: Naaman, afflicted with leprosy, is directed by a young girl to seek healing from Elisha; he washes seven times in the Jordan and is made clean, and comes to know the true God.
keyPoints: Naaman, commander of the Syrian army, is afflicted with leprosy, and a young Israelite girl directs him to the prophet Elisha.
Naaman is at first unwilling to wash in the Jordan, but after his servants urge him, he obeys and is made clean.
Naaman comes to believe in the LORD; Elisha refuses his gifts, and Gehazi is punished for his greed.
chapters.application: Obeying God's simple instructions is often the path to blessing. Let us lay down our pride, receive with humility, and we will surely see God's great power.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how Elisha makes an axe head float, reveals the schemes of the king of Syria, leads a Syrian army into the city and treats them kindly, and prophesies during the famine when Samaria is besieged.
keyPoints: Elisha makes an axe head that had sunk in the water float to the surface, revealing God's great power.
Elisha exposes the military schemes of the king of Syria, and leads a Syrian army into Samaria, yet treats them with kindness.
Samaria is besieged by the Syrian army and famine grips the city severely, but Elisha prophesies that by the next day food will be plentiful.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us believe that God sees and governs all things. He can open our eyes to see the spiritual help around us, and he enables us to treat even our enemies with kindness, so that we become more than conquerors.

chapters.summary: Elisha prophesies that Samaria will be delivered; four lepers discover that the Syrian army has abandoned its camp, the people of the city eat their fill, but the king's captain, because of his unbelief, is trampled to death.
keyPoints: Elisha prophesies that by the next day fine flour and barley will be sold cheaply at the gate of Samaria.
Four lepers venture into the Syrian camp and discover that the enemy has fled, leaving behind their goods and provisions.
Because he does not believe the prophecy, the king's captain is trampled to death by the crowd, fulfilling Elisha's word.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us trust God's promises rather than despair over what we see. God will surely bring deliverance in his own time; let us respond in faith, lest unbelief cause us to miss out on his grace.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the restoration of the Shunammite woman's property, Elisha's prophecy of Ben-hadad's death and the anointing of Hazael as king of Syria, and the wicked deeds of Jehoram and Ahaziah, kings of Judah.
keyPoints: Following Elisha's instructions, the Shunammite woman goes to live in the land of the Philistines, and after seven years her house and field are restored to her.
In the presence of Ben-hadad, Elisha prophesies that he will surely die, and Hazael usurps the throne to become king of Syria.
Jehoram king of Judah does evil, and his son Ahaziah succeeds him; through marriage into the house of Ahab, he too does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.
themes: The corruption of the royal house
chapters.application: However circumstances may change, God watches over those who belong to him. Let us give thanks in good times and rely on him in hard times, holding fast to faith, for God will never forget his promises.

chapters.summary: The prophet Elisha sends someone to anoint Jehu king of Israel; in obedience to God's will Jehu strikes down King Joram and Jezebel, fulfilling God's judgment on the house of Ahab.
keyPoints: Elisha sends one of the sons of the prophets to anoint Jehu, proclaiming God's judgment on the house of Ahab.
Jehu is made king at Ramoth-gilead, and immediately sets out for Jezreel to carry out the judgment.
King Joram and Jezebel are killed, fulfilling the prophecy the LORD spoke through Elijah.
chapters.application: God is righteous, and he will surely judge sin. Let us revere God, turn away from evil, and act faithfully within his will.

chapters.summary: In obedience to God's will Jehu wipes out the house of Ahab and purges the worship of Baal, yet he does not wholeheartedly keep God's law.
keyPoints: After being anointed, Jehu carries out God's judgment on the house of Ahab, killing Joram, Jezebel, and all of Ahab's sons.
By a clever scheme Jehu kills all the worshipers of Baal and destroys the temple of Baal, yet he continues to worship the golden calves.
Because Jehu carries out what is right in God's eyes, God promises that his descendants will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.
chapters.application: God values our complete obedience, not partial commitment. Lord, help us to follow you wholeheartedly, never growing complacent over our achievements, and remain faithful to the very end.

chapters.summary: Athaliah usurps the throne, but Jehoiada makes Joash king and overthrows Athaliah, restoring the Davidic dynasty.
keyPoints: Athaliah destroys the royal family and usurps the throne for six years.
Jehoiada hides Joash away and plans to restore him to the throne.
Joash is anointed king, and Athaliah is put to death.
chapters.application: Even when evil seems to prevail, God is still sovereign behind the scenes. Let us trust his promises and hold fast to the truth in hardship, for he will surely make his righteousness known.

chapters.summary: Under the teaching of the priest Jehoiada, Joash king of Judah repairs the temple, but in his later years he forsakes God and is killed by his own servants.
keyPoints: Joash becomes king at the age of seven, and under Jehoiada's instruction does what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
Joash instructs the priests to use the offered silver to repair the temple, but they delay the work, so the king takes direct oversight until it is completed.
In his later years Joash forsakes God and is betrayed and killed by his own servants; he is buried in the city of David.
chapters.application: Faith must be continually maintained, never allowed to grow slack with circumstances or the passing of time. Let Joash's example warn us to follow the Lord all our lives, until we see his face.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the reigns of Jehoahaz and Jehoash, kings of Israel, Elisha's prophecy before his death, and God's mercy toward Israel.
keyPoints: Jehoahaz does evil, and God allows the Syrians to oppress Israel, but because Jehoahaz repents, God grants a deliverer.
Jehoash continues to do evil, but as Elisha lies dying he prophesies that Israel will defeat Syria three times.
After Elisha dies, a dead man is restored to life when his body touches Elisha's bones, revealing God's great power.
chapters.application: However weak we may be, God is still willing to hear our cries and grant deliverance. Let us turn back to God in hardship, trusting his mercy and his promises.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the reigns of Amaziah king of Judah and Jehoash king of Israel: after defeating Edom, Amaziah grows arrogant and challenges Israel, but is ultimately defeated and captured, and the chapter also records the expansion of Jeroboam II, king of Israel.
keyPoints: Amaziah does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not like David; he allows the high places to remain.
After defeating Edom, Amaziah becomes proud and self-confident and challenges Jehoash king of Israel, leading to Judah's crushing defeat and the breaching of Jerusalem's walls.
Jeroboam II, king of Israel, recovers lost territory, but he does evil; because Israel is suffering, God graciously grants deliverance.
chapters.application: Let Amaziah's example be a warning to us: let us not grow proud and arrogant because of momentary success, but always keep a humble heart, rely on God, and carefully keep his commands, that we may be blessed.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the reigns of Azariah and Jotham, kings of Judah, and the events of Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah, kings of Israel, revealing the political turmoil and spiritual corruption of the northern kingdom.
keyPoints: Azariah king of Judah does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, yet the high places are not removed, and in his later years he is struck with leprosy.
Zechariah king of Israel is assassinated; Shallum usurps the throne, and Menahem in turn kills Shallum, plunging the nation into political chaos.
The king of Assyria invades, and Menahem pays tribute to buy peace; Israel's power continues to decline, and finally Pekah is killed and Jotham succeeds to the throne of Judah.
chapters.application: When society is in turmoil, let us hold fast to a pure faith rather than drifting with the crowd, and with patient endurance and prayer look to God's faithfulness and righteousness amid change.

chapters.summary: Fearing the combined forces of Syria and Israel, Ahaz king of Judah appeals to the king of Assyria for help, and copies an altar he sees in Damascus, changing the worship of the temple and bringing about spiritual decline.
keyPoints: Ahaz does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the ways of the kings of Israel, even making his son pass through the fire.
Facing the siege of the combined forces of Syria and Israel, Ahaz does not rely on God but instead bribes Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria with silver and gold taken from the temple.
When Ahaz sees an altar in Damascus, he has a copy made and commands the priest Urijah to offer sacrifices on it in the temple, changing the manner of worship.
chapters.application: When we face hardship, are we, like Ahaz, quick to seek human help while neglecting God? Lord, grant us faith to call on you first in times of danger, rather than following the ways of the world.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how the northern kingdom of Israel, because of its long history of idolatry and forsaking God, is destroyed by Assyria; the people are carried into exile, foreign peoples are settled in the land, and the mingling of peoples leads to a mixed and corrupted faith.
keyPoints: Hoshea rebels against Assyria, and as a result Samaria is besieged for three years before it falls.
Israel is carried into exile in Assyria because they have sinned against the LORD and worshiped other gods.
The king of Assyria settles foreign peoples in the land; they fear the LORD, yet continue to serve their own gods.
chapters.application: Let us carefully keep God's word and not follow the idols of this world; if we stray from the right path, let us turn back promptly, for though God is merciful, his justice will surely come as well.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how Hezekiah king of Judah does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, abolishes idols, and relies on God; facing the threat of Sennacherib king of Assyria, he responds with faith and prayer.
keyPoints: King Hezekiah comes to the throne and does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, removing the high places, breaking the sacred pillars, and cutting down the Asherah poles.
Hezekiah relies on the LORD and carefully keeps his commandments; the LORD is with him, and he prospers in everything he does.
Sennacherib king of Assyria captures Samaria and then besieges Judah; Hezekiah seeks peace and offers silver and gold, but Assyria continues to threaten Jerusalem.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us, like Hezekiah, rely wholeheartedly on God and keep his word, never shaken by circumstances, for God will surely keep and watch over us.

chapters.summary: Facing the threat of the king of Assyria, King Hezekiah seeks out Isaiah and the LORD in his distress; God declares deliverance through Isaiah and, in a single night, strikes down the Assyrian army, keeping Jerusalem safe.
keyPoints: Hezekiah tears his clothes, goes into the temple, and sends men to inquire of the prophet Isaiah.
Isaiah delivers the word of God, prophesying that the king of Assyria will surely be defeated, and promising that Jerusalem will be protected.
God sends an angel to strike down a hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib is later assassinated.
chapters.application: When we face hardship, let us follow Hezekiah's example, praying to God first and seeking spiritual guidance. God will surely hear our cries and bring deliverance, so that those who trust in him will never be put to shame.

chapters.summary: Hezekiah becomes gravely ill and prays for his life to be extended; God grants him fifteen more years and gives the sign of the shadow going backward, but when Hezekiah shows off his wealth to envoys from Babylon, Isaiah prophesies the coming exile.
keyPoints: Hezekiah, gravely ill, weeps bitterly and prays to God, and God agrees to heal him and add to his life.
God gives the sign of the shadow going back ten steps, showing that his promise is true and can be trusted.
When Hezekiah receives envoys from Babylon he shows off his treasures, and Isaiah declares that Judah will be carried into exile.
chapters.application: In times of prosperity let us remember God's grace and not grow proud or boastful. Let us rely on the Lord with humility in all things, lest showing off cause us to lose his blessing.

chapters.summary: Manasseh king of Judah does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations; God declares judgment through his prophets. After his death his son Amon succeeds him and also does evil, and he is killed by his own servants.
keyPoints: Manasseh rebuilds the altars to idols and worships Baal and all the host of heaven.
God declares through his prophets that he will bring disaster on Jerusalem, wiping it as one wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.
Amon succeeds him and does evil; he is betrayed and killed by his own servants, and the people of the land make his son Josiah king.
chapters.application: Let us be watchful against the spread of sin; even amid a corrupt environment, let us hold fast to a pure faith, for God will surely judge in righteousness, yet he also leaves room for repentance.

chapters.summary: During the reign of King Josiah the Book of the Law is discovered, and he leads the people to renew their covenant with God and carries out religious reform.
keyPoints: Josiah comes to the throne at only eight years old and reigns for thirty-one years, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
While the temple is being repaired the Book of the Law is discovered, and after it is read to him, Josiah tears his clothes, showing his deep repentance.
Josiah gathers the people, reads the Book of the Law aloud, and makes a covenant with God to obey the LORD with all his heart and all his soul.
chapters.application: When God's word is rediscovered, it brings renewal. Let us read Scripture regularly, receive it with humility, respond to God's teaching in action, and live out a godly life.

chapters.summary: King Josiah carries out religious reform in Jerusalem, removing idols, restoring the Passover, and renewing the covenant.
keyPoints: Josiah gathers the people, reads aloud the Book of the Law, and makes a covenant with God.
He abolishes the idols throughout the land, tears down the high places, and purifies the temple.
He keeps the Passover according to the Law; his reform is thorough, and it pleases God.
chapters.application: Let us follow Josiah's example, removing the idols in our hearts, renewing our resolve to obey God's word, and living a holy life from this day forward.

chapters.summary: During the reigns of Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin, kings of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon captures Jerusalem; Judah falls, and the people are carried into exile.
keyPoints: Jehoiakim submits to Babylon for three years and then rebels, bringing attacks from Babylon and the surrounding nations.
After Jehoiakim dies, his son Jehoiachin succeeds him, but Jerusalem is besieged, and Jehoiachin surrenders and is carried into exile.
The king of Babylon carries off the treasures of the temple and the palace, and takes away the elite of Judah into exile, leaving behind only the poorest of the people.
chapters.application: When we drift far from God, we may fall into hardship. But God still governs history, and his discipline is meant to bring us back. In adversity, let us examine our hearts and turn to God.

chapters.summary: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon captures Jerusalem; Judah falls, the temple is destroyed, the people are carried into exile, and the kingdom of Judah comes to an end.
keyPoints: Babylon besieges Jerusalem, and when the city falls, King Zedekiah is captured; his sons are killed before his eyes, he is then blinded, and he is carried off to Babylon.
The temple, the palace, and the walls of Jerusalem are burned, the vessels of the temple are plundered, and the priests and leaders are put to death.

The people of Judah are carried into exile, leaving only the poorest to tend the vineyards and fields; Gedaliah is appointed governor but is later assassinated, and the remaining people flee to Egypt.
chapters.application: When failure and loss come, let us remember God's justice and faithfulness. Let us hold on to hope even in hardship, for God has a plan for restoration.
